title: Attention Is All You Need: Core Argument Plan
subtitle: From Sequential Constraints to Parallel Self-Attention Dominance

nodes.title: Limitations of Sequential Models
nodes.purpose: Establish the fundamental bottleneck of RNNs/CNNs: sequential computation prevents parallelization and hinders learning long-range dependencies due to path length.

nodes.title: The Transformer Architecture Proposal
nodes.purpose: Introduce the core claim: a model relying entirely on attention mechanisms, dispensing with recurrence and convolutions, to achieve superior parallelizability and performance.

nodes.title: Scaled Dot-Product Attention Mechanism
nodes.purpose: Define the mathematical foundation: Attention(Q,K,V) = softmax(QK^T/sqrt(dk))V. Explain the scaling factor 1/sqrt(dk) as a countermeasure against vanishing gradients in high dimensions.

nodes.title: Multi-Head Attention Strategy
nodes.purpose: Explain the mechanism of projecting queries, keys, and values into multiple subspaces (h=8, dk=dv=64) to jointly attend to information from different representation positions.

nodes.title: Positional Encoding Injection
nodes.purpose: Address the lack of recurrence by injecting order information via sine/cosine functions (PE formulas), enabling the model to utilize sequence order without learned embeddings.

nodes.title: Computational Complexity & Path Length Analysis
nodes.purpose: Provide theoretical justification comparing Self-Attention vs. Recurrent vs. Convolutional layers regarding operations per layer (O(n^2*d)), sequential operations (O(1)), and maximum path length (O(1)).

nodes.title: Training Configuration and Optimization
nodes.purpose: Detail the specific training conditions required for success: Adam optimizer, variable learning rate schedule (warmup + inverse square root), and regularization techniques (Dropout, Label Smoothing).

nodes.title: Machine Translation State-of-the-Art Results
nodes.purpose: Present empirical evidence: WMT 2014 En-De (28.4 BLEU) and En-Fr (41.8 BLEU) scores, demonstrating superiority over ensembles at a fraction of the training cost (FLOPs).

nodes.title: Architecture Ablation and Sensitivity
nodes.purpose: Validate design choices through Table 3 variations: impact of head count, key dimension (dk), model size, and the equivalence of learned vs. sinusoidal positional encodings.

nodes.title: Generalization to Constituency Parsing
nodes.purpose: Demonstrate task agnosticism by applying the Transformer to English constituency parsing (WSJ), achieving competitive F1 scores (92.7 semi-supervised) without task-specific tuning.

coverage_notes: The argument flows logically from the problem of sequential constraints (Node 1) to the proposed solution (Node 2), detailed mechanics (Nodes 3-5), theoretical benefits (Node 6), implementation specifics (Node 7), and finally empirical validation across tasks (Nodes 8-10).
Visual evidence in Appendix (Pages 13-15) supports the claim of interpretability and long-distance dependency modeling but is treated as supplementary to the core quantitative results.
The distinction between 'Base' and 'Big' models is critical in the results section to separate architectural validity from scale benefits.
